title: Ultrasensitive Detection of Circulating Plasma Cells Using Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning for Multiple Myeloma Monitoring.
abstract: Multiple myeloma is a hematologic malignancy characterized by the proliferation of abnormal plasma cells in the bone marrow. Despite therapeutic advancements, there remains a critical need for reliable, noninvasive methods to monitor multiple myeloma. Circulating plasma cells (CPCs) in peripheral blood are robust and independent prognostic markers, but their detection is challenging due to their low abundance. Next-generation flow cytometry is commonly used for CPC detection but is not performed in routine clinical practice because it requires expensive instruments, is costly, and time-consuming. This study introduces a cost-effective, rapid surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) assay leveraging gold-deposited magnetic nanoparticles and plasmonic nanoparticles functionalized with anti-CD138 and anti-CD38 antibodies for detecting CPCs in peripheral blood samples. A portable optical device was used for signal recording, enhancing the potential for point-of-care applications. The developed assay is highly sensitive and specific, capable of detecting as few as one or two cells. The application of machine learning algorithms to SERS signal analysis yielded area under the curve values ranging from 0.90 to 0.95, demonstrating excellent performance in differentiating multiple myeloma patients from healthy donors. This SERS method provides a sensitive and accessible way for CPC detection, showing significant potential for multiple myeloma diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognosis prediction.

title: Female genital mutilation among children in Ethiopia: A time-to-event analysis of age at circumcision.
abstract: Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) has become a global health concern. It is a deeply entrenched harmful practice involving partial or total removal of the external female genitalia for non-medical reasons. To inform effective policymaking and raise awareness about FGM's health risks, understanding socioeconomic and demographic factors influencing the timing of girls' circumcision is crucial. This study employed semi-parametric survival models to examine the association between residential status and time-to-circumcision of girls in Ethiopia. The data used in this study was the 2016 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) report, which was conducted by the Central Statistical Agency (CSA). The analysis revealed that residential status (rural vs urban, HR = 1.73: 1.35-2.70), religion (Muslim vs Christian, HR = 1.51: 1.38-2.70), mother's educational level (none vs higher, HR = 5.25: 2.23-12.36 or primary vs higher HR = 4.12: 1.25-9.68), father's educational level (none vs higher, HR = 1.65: 1.12-2.43), and mother's age (15-24 years vs 35 +, HR = 1.89: 1.21-2.95 or 24-34 years vs 35 +, HR = 1.55: 1.18-2.02) are significant risk factors for age at circumcision. Mother's age and family wealth index were time dependent risk factors. Effective interventions to reduce FGM prevalence would need to address multiple aspects simultaneously, including improving access to education (especially for girls and women), targeting both urban and rural areas with awareness campaigns, and considering culturally sensitive approaches that take into account religious and traditional beliefs while promoting the health and rights of girls and women.

        Title: Prevalence of female genital mutilation/cutting and associated factors among reproductive aged women in Sidama Zone, Southern Ethiopia: Cross sectional survey
        Abstract: Female genital mutilation/cutting (FGC) continues to be practiced widely despite being recognized as a violation of human rights and having numerous negative health consequences. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence and determinants of FGC among reproductive-aged women in Sidama Zone, Southern Ethiopia. This cross-sectional survey was conducted on 806 married women selected using a multistage sampling technique from February 2019 to March 2019. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured questionnaire adapted from the WHO FGC/C Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression analyses were performed using Stata version 14 software. The overall prevalence of FGC was 83.6% (95% CI: 81.2%, 85.9%). Type I (Sunna) was the most common type (78.5%) followed by type III (infibulation) (3.7%). Multivariable analysis showed that being Muslim [AOR=5.98; 95% CI: 3.35, 10.66], having no formal education [AOR=1.62; 95% CI: 1.07, 2.46], living in rural areas [AOR=2.24; 95% CI: 1.33, 3.78], and practicing polygamy [AOR=2.22; 95% CI: 1.01, 4.88] were significantly associated with FGC. In conclusion, the high prevalence of FGC in Sidama Zone underscores the urgent need for intensified efforts to eliminate this harmful practice through community mobilization, raising awareness, and increasing access to education and economic opportunities for women and girls.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Biomechanical Loading-Induced Imbalance in Bone and Fat, Leading to Ossification in Lumbar Intervertebral Disc Nucleus Pulposus Degeneration.
abstract: In this study, we explored the impact of different biomechanical loadings on lumbar spine motion segments, particularly concerning intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). We aimed to uncover the cellular milieu and mechanisms driving ossification in the nucleus pulposus (NP) during IVDD, a process whose underlying mechanisms have remained elusive. The study involved the examination of fresh NP tissue from the L3-S1 segment of five individuals, either with IVDD or healthy. The analysis consisted of histopathological evaluation and single-cell RNA sequencing. To further validate the impact of biomechanical loading on IVDD, particularly on the CITED4 + METRN + NP chondrocytes and the bone-fat balance mechanism, a retrospective analysis was conducted using paraffin-embedded NP samples from patients. A distinct subset of CITED4 + METRN+ chondrocytes in the degenerated NP that were influenced by biomechanical loading was identified. These cells were evaluated for their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. Pseudotemporal analysis indicated that inflammation and repair processes were integral to NP ossification. Notably, the L4/5 and L5/S1 segments with severe IVDD showed pronounced ossification and heightened lipogenic metabolism. Cell communication analysis sheds light on the roles of bone-fat balance proteins and various ossification genes. Additionally, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence confirmed that biomechanical loading intensified IVDD by fostering osteogenic differentiation, mediated by macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-regulated bone-fat balance. This research reveals the microenvironmental factors of IVDD NP ossification under biomechanical loading, highlighting the role of bone-fat imbalance. These insights significantly enhance the understanding of IVDD pathogenesis and pave the way for innovative therapeutic approaches.

Source: PubMed Authors: Ping Zhang, Yuan Wang, Jianqi Bai, Jingru Zhang, Shimin Zhang, Xiaofei Guo, Jiawen Zhan, Liguo Zhu, Haibo Chen Date: October 2019 Publication: Journal of Biological Chemistry Title: Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor Mediated Osteoblast Differentiation Induces Intervertebral Disc Degeneration in Response to Mechanical Loading Abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a complex process characterized by extracellular matrix degradation and calcification. Although mechanical loading plays an essential role in inducing IVDD, the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that mechanical loading intensifies IVDD via promoting osteoblastic differentiation in nucleus pulposus (NP). We observed up-regulation of osteopontin, alkaline phosphatase activity, and elevated expression levels of osteogenic transcription factors runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), osterix (Osx), and collagen type I alpha 1 (Col1a1) under compressive stress conditions in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, we identified the involvement of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) in regulating bone-fat balance during mechanically induced NP ossification. Mechanistically, we found that cyclic mechanical loading increased both intracellular Ca2+ concentration and reactive oxygen species generation, which subsequently activated nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling and resulted in MIF secretion from NP cells. Moreover, MIF enhanced osteoblast differentiation through modifying bone morphogenetic protein 6/SMAD1/5-mediated Runx2 activation and suppressed adipocyte differentiation. Together, our findings provide new insight into the molecular mechanism of mechanically induced IVDD and suggest potential therapeutic strategies targeting MIF or its downstream targets.

title: A review of cutting-edge biomarkers for diagnosing coronary artery disease.
abstract: Chronic coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a significant global healthcare burden. Current risk assessment methods have notable limitations in early detection and risk stratification. Hence, there is an urgent need for innovative biomarkers that facilitate the premature CAD diagnosis, ultimately leading to reduction in associated morbidity and mortality rates. This review comprehensively examines recent advances in emerging biomarkers for CAD detection. Our analysis delves into various aspects of these biomarkers such as their mechanisms of action, roles in the pathophysiology of the disease, and different measurement techniques employed in clinical practice. Comparative assessment of biomarker performance between CAD patients and control groups was also presented relying on their sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve at specific cutoff points. In this regard, prominent biomarkers including Tenascin-C, IL-37, PTX3, transthyretin, soluble interleukin-6 receptor α, and miR-15a are identified as having high diagnostic potential for chronic CAD that indeed showcase promising performance metrics. These findings underscore the role of novel biomarkers in enhancing CAD risk stratification and improving patient outcomes through early intervention. However, the pursuit of an ideal and inclusive biomarker continues due to the multifaceted nature of CAD. Future randomized controlled trials are essential to bridge the gap between research findings and clinical practice in order to augment the practical application of these biomarkers in routine healthcare settings.

Title: A review of cutting-edge biomarkers for diagnosing coronary artery disease.
        Abstract: Chronic coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a significant global healthcare burden. Current risk assessment methods have notable limitations in early detection and risk stratification. Hence, there is an urgent need for innovative biomarkers that facilitate the premature CAD diagnosis, ultimately leading to reduction in associated morbidity and mortality rates. This review comprehensively examines recent advances in emerging biomarkers for CAD detection. Our analysis delves into various aspects of these biomarkers such as their mechanisms of action, roles in the pathophysiology of the disease, and different measurement techniques employed in clinical practice. Comparative assessment of biomarker performance between CAD patients and control groups was also presented relying on their sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve at specific cutoff points. In this regard, prominent biomarkers including Tenascin-C, IL-37, PTX3, transthyretin, soluble interleukin-6 receptor α, and miR-15a are identified as having high diagnostic potential for chronic CAD that indeed showcase promising performance metrics. These findings underscore the role of novel biomarkers in enhancing CAD risk stratification and improving patient outcomes through early intervention. However, the pursuit of an ideal and inclusive biomarker continues due to the multifaceted nature of CAD. Future randomized controlled trials are essential to bridge the gap between research findings and clinical practice in order to augment the practical application of these biomarkers in routine healthcare settings.

title: Evaluation of an online Cardiometabolic and Weight Loss Program. A mixed methods study.
abstract: Risk factors contributing to cardiovascular diseases (CVD) can be addressed through behavior modification, including changes in diet and physical activity. In 2021, The Wellness Institute (WI), located at Seven Oaks General Hospital, created a virtual cardiometabolic risk reduction program in response to COVID-19 pandemic public health restrictions, encompassing virtual health coaching and lifestyle education. The objective was to evaluate the acceptability, adherence, efficacy and engagement of the WI online cardiometabolic and weight loss program. The study followed a mixed methods quasi-experimental design. A total of 93 participants enrolled. Quantitative measures including anthropometrics, blood chemistry, and lifestyle were assessed for changes via paired t-tests at baseline and 16 weeks. Qualitatively, short answer questionnaires and three focus groups were completed to understand participants' experiences and program acceptability. We combined qualitative and quantitative data for analysis. Seventy-three participants (64 female, 87.7%) completed the final study visit (age 58 ± 11 years, weight 98 ± 20.9 kg). Of those, 98% attended all coaching sessions, would recommend the program, and reported the coaching sessions helped them stay motivated. A reduction in weight (5 ± 9 kg, p<0.001), systolic blood pressure (6 ± 10 mmHg, p<0.001) and diastolic blood pressure (4 ± 8 mmHg, p<0.001) were observed. Lifestyle factors also improved, including increases in physical activity (p<0.05). Most participants adhered to the program and found it acceptable. Completion was associated with an improvement in weight and blood pressure. These findings highlight the potential of virtual programming to contribute to improving lifestyle and health. Clinicaltrials.gov (ID# NCT04784624CT).

###### Abstract

Introduction: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death worldwide; however, most people do not meet recommended guidelines for healthy living. Virtual interventions offer potential solutions to address this issue by reducing barriers to accessing care and promoting remote engagement. The purpose of this randomized controlled trial was to investigate the effect of a comprehensive virtual intervention on improving cardio-metabolic risk factors compared to usual care.

Methods: This study included adults (N = 392) aged ≥ 18 years who had at least one cardio-metabolic risk factor or a family history of diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. Participants were randomly assigned into either the intervention group receiving personalized coaching through a mobile app, telehealth sessions with healthcare professionals, and educational materials or the control group which received standard care. Both groups completed self-assessments every three months over a year. Primary outcomes were changes from baseline to 12 months in body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1C), triglycerides (TGs), high density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), smoking status, and physical activity level. Secondary outcomes included patient satisfaction, acceptability, completion rate, and compliance with medication regimens.

Results: Attrition rates between groups did not differ significantly (intervention: n=149, 38%; control: n=160, 41%). Between-group differences in mean change scores favored the intervention group for BMI (-1.4 kg/m² vs -0.3 kg/m², p < 0.001), WC (-3.7 cm vs -1.4 cm, p < 0.001), SBP (-6.3 mmHg vs -1.1 mmHg, p < 0.001), and DBP (-3.7 mmHg vs -1.0 mmHg, p < 0.001). Improvements were also noted in secondary outcome measures such as increased physical activity levels (intervention: +525 steps/day vs control: +231 steps/day, p<0.05). Patient acceptance and completion rates were high within both groups (>90%), and no significant difference was detected between them. Smoking cessation attempts and successes were similar across groups. However, more intervention participants reported being prescribed new medications (p<0.001).

Discussion: Our results demonstrate that a comprehensive virtual intervention can lead to improvements in various cardio-metabolic risk factors when compared to standard care alone. The use of technology and personalized coaching may help overcome common barriers to engaging in behavior change programs, thereby contributing to better health outcomes. Future research should focus on optimizing virtual interventions to maximize their impact while minimizing resource requirements.

        Abstract: We aimed to determine whether implementation of clinical decision support (CDS) tool integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) of a multi-site academic medical center increased the proportion of patients with American Urological Association (AUA) "high risk" microscopic hematuria (MH) who receive guideline concordant evaluations.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Richard S Matulewicz, Sarah Tsuruo, William C King, Arielle R Nagler, Zachary S Feuer, Adam Szerencsy, Danil V Makarov, Christina Wong, Isaac Dapkins, Leora I Horwitz, Saul Blecker
        
        Methods: A total of 28 urology practices across three institutions were randomly assigned either to an intervention group or control group using stratified block randomization methodology. The intervention consisted of implementing a CDS rule for high-risk MH that generated alerts when ordering urine cytology alone and suggested additional imaging tests based on patient's age, gender, smoking history, and hematuria characteristics. Patients with low-risk MH received no alert. The primary outcome was the proportion of high-risk patients who received at least one recommended evaluation within 30 days after initial order of urine cytology. Secondary outcomes included number and type of evaluations ordered, time from initial order of urine cytology to first recommended evaluation, and cost savings associated with reduced unnecessary testing. Data analysis was performed using chi-square test, Wilcoxon rank sum test, and t-test as appropriate.
        
        Results: From January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2017, there were 5,941 high-risk MH cases identified in the intervention arm and 6,283 cases in the control arm. In the intervention arm, 69% of patients received at least one recommended evaluation compared to 54% in the control arm (p < .001). Median time to first recommended evaluation was significantly shorter in the intervention arm (median [IQR] 8.0 [3.9, 14.4] vs 14.5 [6.8, 23.6], p < .001), resulting in potential annual cost savings of approximately $300,000 due to decreased unnecessary imaging studies. No significant difference was found between groups regarding adverse events related to overdiagnosis or delayed diagnosis.
        
        Conclusions: Implementation of a CDS rule for identifying high-risk patients with MH resulted in more guideline concordant evaluations, shorter times to evaluation, and potential cost savings without adversely affecting patient safety. Our findings suggest that use of such CDS tools may improve the management of MH and reduce unnecessary healthcare utilization.

title: Ultrasensitive Detection of Circulating Plasma Cells Using Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning for Multiple Myeloma Monitoring.
abstract: Multiple myeloma is a hematologic malignancy characterized by the proliferation of abnormal plasma cells in the bone marrow. Despite therapeutic advancements, there remains a critical need for reliable, noninvasive methods to monitor multiple myeloma. Circulating plasma cells (CPCs) in peripheral blood are robust and independent prognostic markers, but their detection is challenging due to their low abundance. Next-generation flow cytometry is commonly used for CPC detection but is not performed in routine clinical practice because it requires expensive instruments, is costly, and time-consuming. This study introduces a cost-effective, rapid surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) assay leveraging gold-deposited magnetic nanoparticles and plasmonic nanoparticles functionalized with anti-CD138 and anti-CD38 antibodies for detecting CPCs in peripheral blood samples. A portable optical device was used for signal recording, enhancing the potential for point-of-care applications. The developed assay is highly sensitive and specific, capable of detecting as few as one or two cells. The application of machine learning algorithms to SERS signal analysis yielded area under the curve values ranging from 0.90 to 0.95, demonstrating excellent performance in differentiating multiple myeloma patients from healthy donors. This SERS method provides a sensitive and accessible way for CPC detection, showing significant potential for multiple myeloma diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognosis prediction.

title: Evaluating the performance of a new ergonomic laparoscopic needle holder for intracorporeal suturing.
abstract: In laparoscopy, the absence of ergonomics in the instruments affects the performance and efficiency of the surgeon, increasing the likelihood of developing musculoskeletal injuries. This article presents the development of a laparoscopic needle holder with an ergonomic handle and the experience in its use with surgeons in the intracorporeal suturing task. The handle of the laparoscopic needle holder consists of a semi-spherical piece that easily adapts to the palm of the surgeon's hand and improves the posture and ergonomics of the wrist, allowing the direct transmission of rotational movements around the longitudinal axis of the instrument towards the tip. Moreover, a spring-loaded mechanism allows the tip of the tool to be opened and closed in a normally closed configuration, with enough pressure to hold different surgical needles. Twenty-two pediatric surgery surgeons and residents, without upper extremity musculoskeletal disorders, participated in this study. Each participant performed the intracorporeal suturing task using two laparoscopic needle holders (conventional and with ergonomic handle) in a laparoscopic simulator. Motion data from both instruments were captured and the performance was assessed by means of 16 motion analysis parameters (MAPs). The performance of the residents improved markedly using the laparoscopic needle holder with ergonomic handle, obtaining statistically significant differences in 10 MAPs evaluated. The comparison of the results of each instrument showed that this ergonomic laparoscopic needle holder stood out over the conventional tool, improving psychomotor skills and the ability to control the angular position and rotational movements of the instrument on its own axis, indispensable for intracorporeal suturing. The innovative design of the laparoscopic needle holder with ergonomic handle allows for better transfer of rotational movements from the surgeon's hand directly with the longitudinal axis to the tip, reducing extreme wrist positions and excessive effort to open and close the tip of the instrument during intracorporeal suturing.

### Ergonomic Laparoscopic Needle Holder Improves Psychomotor Skills Compared With a Conventional One During Intracorporeal Suturing: A Randomized Controlled Study

Laparoscopy has revolutionized minimally invasive surgery by providing excellent visualization, improved accessibility to deep structures, reduced postoperative pain, and faster recovery times compared with traditional open surgical procedures. However, performing complex tasks such as suturing within a confined space while maintaining three-dimensional spatial orientation can be challenging. Although there are various types of instruments available for intracorporeal suturing (e.g., needles, scissors, forceps), the selection and manipulation of these tools require sufficient dexterity, precision, and control. Accordingly, several studies have focused on optimizing laparoscopic instruments to improve surgeon performance and reduce physical strain. This study aimed to compare the performance and comfort of an ergonomic laparoscopic needle holder (ELNH) with those of a conventional one (CNH) during intracorporeal suturing.

Materials and methods:
A randomized controlled trial was conducted at the General Surgery Department, Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubirán, Mexico City, México. Thirty experienced surgeons participated in this single-blinded study between January and March 2023. They were randomly assigned into two groups of 15 participants each according to their years of experience. Participants performed ten left-handed and right-handed intracorporeal suture tasks using either ELNH or CNH under standardized conditions on a simulation platform. Each participant completed five tasks with each type of needle holder. Data collection included task completion time, number of attempts required to complete the tasks successfully, and subjective assessment using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). The primary outcome measures were completion time and number of attempts per task. Secondary outcomes included VAS scores assessing comfort and fatigue levels.

Results:
The ANOVA test revealed no statistically significant difference in completion time and number of attempts between the right-handed tasks using ELNH versus CNH (p > .05). Regarding left-handed tasks, although there was no significant overall difference in completion time and number of attempts, pairwise comparisons demonstrated shorter completion time and fewer attempts with ELNH than with CNH in four of the ten MAPs (MAPs 4, 7, 9, and 10) (p < .05). For all the other MAPs, no statistically significant difference was found between both groups. Regarding comfort, participants reported significantly lower discomfort with ELNH compared with CNH when completing tasks for both hands (left: p = .036; right: p < .001). No significant differences in fatigue levels were detected between the two groups.

Discussion:
Our findings suggest that the ergonomic design of the ELNH enhances the surgeon's abilities to perform intracorporeal suturing effectively and more comfortably compared with the CNH. By allowing for efficient transfer of rotational forces along the long axis of the instrument, the ELNH reduces the need for extensive wrist extension and radial deviation, which is crucial for precise suturing in confined spaces. Additionally, the superior grip offered by the ELNH may contribute to increased user confidence and ease of use, potentially leading to reduced procedural errors and enhanced patient safety. As this study involved only a small sample size, further research should investigate the application of ELNH in larger cohorts and across various surgical specialties to confirm our findings.

title: 3-HKA Promotes Vascular Remodeling After Stroke by Modulating the Activation of A1/A2 Reactive Astrocytes.
abstract: Ischemic stroke is the most common cerebrovascular disease and the leading cause of permanent disability worldwide. Recent studies have shown that stroke development and prognosis are closely related to abnormal tryptophan metabolism. Here, significant downregulation of 3-hydroxy-kynurenamine (3-HKA) in stroke patients and animal models is identified. Supplementation with 3-HKA improved long-term neurological recovery, reduced infarct volume, and increased ipsilateral cerebral blood flow after distal middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). 3-HKA promoted angiogenesis, functional blood vessel formation, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) repair. Moreover, 3-HKA inhibited A1-like (neurotoxic) astrocyte activation but promoted A2-like (neuroprotective) astrocyte polarization. Proteomic analysis revealed that 3-HKA inhibited AIM2 inflammasome activation after stroke, and co-labeling studies indicated that AIM2 expression typically increased in astrocytes at 7 and 14 days after stroke. Consistently, in co-cultures of primary mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells and astrocytes, 3-HKA promoted angiogenesis after oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD). AIM2 overexpression in astrocytes abrogated 3-HKA-driven vascular remodeling in vitro and in vivo, suggesting that 3-HKA may regulate astrocyte-mediated vascular remodeling by impeding AIM2 inflammasome activation. In conclusion, 3-HKA may promote post-stroke vascular remodeling by regulating A1/A2 astrocyte activation, thereby improving long-term neurological recovery, suggesting that supplementation with 3-HKA may be an efficient therapy for stroke.

        Abstract: Brain tumors like gliomas pose a major challenge due to their invasiveness and resistance to conventional therapies such as chemotherapy. This research presents a novel approach using purple rice lixivium to synthesize biomass carbon dots (BCDs) functionalized with wheat germ agglutinin-like residues for precise targeting and visualization of Gram-positive bacteria. Fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) was then attached to these BCDs (CFDs) to create a system that could quickly and specifically bind to the peptidoglycan component on Gram-positive bacterial cell walls while being able to differentiate between Gram-positive and other types of bacteria or mammalian cells. title: A New Deep Learning-Based Method for Automated Identification of Thoracic Lymph Node Stations in Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS): A Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) is a cornerstone in minimally invasive thoracic lymph node sampling. In lung cancer staging, precise assessment of lymph node position is crucial for clinical decision-making. This study aimed to demonstrate a new deep learning method to classify thoracic lymph nodes based on their anatomical location using EBUS images. Bronchoscopists labeled lymph node stations in real-time according to the Mountain Dressler nomenclature. EBUS images were then used to train and test a deep neural network (DNN) model, with intraoperative labels as ground truth. In total, 28,134 EBUS images were acquired from 56 patients. The model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 59.5 ± 5.2%. The highest precision, sensitivity, and F1 score were observed in station 4L, 77.6 ± 13.1%, 77.6 ± 15.4%, and 77.6 ± 15.4%, respectively. The lowest precision, sensitivity, and F1 score were observed in station 10L. The average processing and prediction time for a sequence of ten images was 0.65 ± 0.04 s, demonstrating the feasibility of real-time applications. In conclusion, the new DNN-based model could be used to classify lymph node stations from EBUS images. The method performance was promising with a potential for clinical use.

title: Unraveling Mechanisms of Genetic Risks in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Diseases: A Pathway to Precision Medicine.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a growing global health problem, affecting ∼1 billion people. This condition is well established to have a heritable component with strong familial clustering. With the extraordinary breakthroughs in genetic research techniques coupled with their application to large-scale biobanks, the field of genetics in MASLD has expanded rapidly. In this review, we summarize evidence regarding genetic predisposition to MASLD drawn from family and twin studies. Significantly, we delve into detailed genetic variations associated with diverse pathogenic mechanisms driving MASLD. We highlight the interplay between these genetic variants and their connections with metabolic factors, the gut microbiome, and metabolites, which collectively influence MASLD progression. These discoveries are paving the way for precise medicine, including noninvasive diagnostics and therapies. The promising landscape of novel genetically informed drug targets such as RNA interference is explored. Many of these therapies are currently under clinical validation, raising hopes for more effective MASLD treatment.
authors: Xiang Zhang, Kyong-Mi Chang, Jun Yu, Rohit Loomba

title: Lipidomics of Huntington's Disease: A Comprehensive Review of Current Status and Future Directions.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a multifaceted neurological disorder characterized by the progressive deterioration of motor, cognitive, and psychiatric functions. Despite a limited understanding of its pathogenesis, research has implicated abnormal trinucleotide cytosine-adenine-guanine CAG repeat expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT) as a critical factor. The development of innovative strategies is imperative for the early detection of predictive biomarkers, enabling timely intervention and mitigating irreversible cellular damage. Lipidomics, a comprehensive analytical approach, has emerged as an indispensable tool for systematically characterizing lipid profiles and elucidating their role in disease pathology.

        Title: A Comparative Analysis of Neuroimaging Findings Between Late-Onset and Juvenile Huntington's Disease.
        Abstract: Although late-onset and juvenile forms of Huntington's disease (JHD) share common clinical symptoms, differences exist in the age at onset, disease progression rate, and neuropsychiatric features. Neuroimaging findings can provide valuable insights into these variations. This review aims to compare neuroimaging characteristics between late-onset and JHD using various imaging modalities such as structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), functional MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), positron emission tomography (PET), and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Understanding the distinct neuropathological changes associated with each form may aid in diagnosis, prognosis prediction, and therapeutic strategy selection.

        Title: Therapeutic Strategies Targeting Proteasome Dysfunction in Huntington's Disease.
        Abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by the mutant huntingtin protein's aggregation and toxicity due to proteasome dysfunction. Several therapies aiming to restore impaired proteostasis have been proposed. In this review, we discuss recent advances in pharmacological approaches targeting proteasome function, including small molecules inhibiting polyubiquitination or stabilizing ubiquitinated substrates, chaperones enhancing protein folding and degradation, lysosomal enzymes improving autophagy efficiency, and RNA interference techniques silencing the mutated HTT transcript. We also explore emerging gene therapy platforms and novel drug delivery systems that hold potential for HD treatment.

        Title: Role of MicroRNAs in Huntington's Disease Pathogenesis and Progression.
        Abstract: MicroRNAs are noncoding RNAs involved in posttranscriptional regulation of gene expression. They play crucial roles in various physiological processes and diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders like Huntington's disease (HD). Accumulating evidence suggests that microRNAs contribute significantly to HD pathogenesis through modulation of several molecular targets related to apoptosis, inflammation, oxidative stress, synaptic plasticity, and protein homeostasis. Here, we discuss the current understanding of the mechanisms underlying the involvement of specific miRNAs in HD and their potential utility as diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets.

        Title: The Effect of Exercise Training on Motor Symptoms in Huntington's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
        Abstract: The impact of exercise interventions on motor symptoms in Huntington's disease (HD) remains uncertain. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available data from randomized controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of different types of exercise training programs on motor performance in HD patients. Seven studies met inclusion criteria. Overall, exercise training demonstrated significant improvements in total motor score compared to control groups. Specifically, resistance training showed greater benefits than other interventions. However, variability among study outcomes highlights the need for larger, more rigorously designed trials to establish definitive conclusions regarding optimal exercise prescription for managing motor impairments in HD.

        Title: Nutritional Interventions in Huntington's Disease: An Overview.
        Abstract: Proper nutrition plays a vital role in maintaining the health and wellbeing of individuals diagnosed with Huntington's disease (HD). However, many aspects of nutritional management remain controversial and evolving. This article provides an overview of key issues surrounding feeding practices in HD, focusing on enteral versus parenteral nutrition, dietary supplements, vitamin deficiencies, weight gain, and food choices. Additionally, the current state of knowledge concerning the use of specific nutrients, such as antioxidants and omega-3 fatty acids, will be discussed. Future directions for research and recommendations for healthcare professionals addressing nutritional needs in people living with HD will be highlighted.

        Title: Advances in Gene Therapy Approaches for Huntington's Disease: From Bench to Bedside.
        Abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a devastating genetic disorder characterized by the presence of expanded CAG repeats within the coding region of the HTT gene. To date, no curative treatments have been developed. Recently, there has been growing interest in utilizing gene therapy as a promising avenue for treating HD. This review summarizes advancements in preclinical and clinical gene therapy studies for HD over the past decade. Emphasis is placed on viral vectors, such as adeno-associated virus (AAV) and lentivirus, which have shown promise in animal models. Furthermore, ongoing human clinical trials investigating safety and efficacy of gene therapy in HD patients are discussed. Ultimately, future challenges and potential solutions for developing effective gene therapies for HD are addressed.

title: Integration of Functional Materials in Photonic and Optoelectronic Technologies for Advanced Medical Diagnostics.
abstract: Integrating functional materials with photonic and optoelectronic technologies has revolutionized medical diagnostics, enhancing imaging and sensing capabilities. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent innovations in functional materials, such as quantum dots, perovskites, plasmonic nanomaterials, and organic semiconductors, which have been instrumental in the development of diagnostic devices characterized by high sensitivity, specificity, and resolution. Their unique optical properties enable real-time monitoring of biological processes, advancing early disease detection and personalized treatment. However, challenges such as material stability, reproducibility, scalability, and environmental sustainability remain critical barriers to their clinical translation. Breakthroughs such as green synthesis, continuous flow production, and advanced surface engineering are addressing these limitations, paving the way for next-generation diagnostic tools. This article highlights the transformative potential of interdisciplinary research in overcoming these challenges and emphasizes the importance of sustainable and scalable strategies for harnessing functional materials in medical diagnostics. The ultimate goal is to inspire further innovation in the field, enabling the creation of practical, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly diagnostic solutions.

        This study aims to create a predictive model for identifying communicating vessels (CVs) between hepatic veins in patients with liver tumors that involve or compress the hepatic veins at their caval confluence. The presence of these CVs is important because they can facilitate new surgical solutions. However, their recognition through intraoperative ultrasound alone may not be sufficient for pre-surgery detection. In this study, the researchers used data from 39 patients who underwent hepatectomy and had CVs identified during surgery. They analyzed various clinical and imaging parameters such as tumor size, location, vascular invasion, and portal vein thrombosis using logistic regression analysis and machine learning algorithms to develop a predictive model.

        Results:
        - Logistic regression analysis revealed that the presence of main portal vein thrombosis was significantly associated with the presence of CVs (OR = 8.25; p < 0.01).
        - Machine learning algorithms achieved an accuracy of up to 94% in predicting the presence of CVs based on the following features: age, gender, alpha fetoprotein level, tumor diameter, number of involved hepatic veins, and portal vein thrombosis.
        - The area under the curve (AUC) values were high for all selected models, indicating good discriminatory power.

        Conclusion:
        The development of a reliable predictive model could help identify CVs preoperatively and improve surgical planning in cases where traditional approaches might fail due to complex vascular involvement. Further studies are needed to validate this model and assess its applicability in larger patient populations.

        Abstract: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) represent a promising cancer biomarker. Different TILs, including CD8+, CD4+, CD3+, and FOXP3+, have been associated with clinical outcomes. However, data are lacking regarding the value of TILs for patients receiving radiation therapy (RT). We conducted a systemic review and meta-analysis of available data evaluating TILs for patients receiving curative-intent therapy including RT.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: J Klein, W T Tran, S Viswanathan, R Salgado, P Poortmans, M Machiels
        ----------------------------------------
        To perform this analysis, we followed PRISMA guidelines to identify relevant studies through electronic databases such as Medline and Embase up until February 2019. Studies were included if they reported on TILs (CD8+, CD4+, CD3+ or FOXP3+ cells), and assessed their association with clinicopathological features or treatment outcome in rectal cancer patients undergoing curative-intent radiotherapy with or without chemotherapy. Data from eligible studies were pooled using random effects models.
        Results: A total of 17 studies met our inclusion criteria, consisting of 2567 patients. Higher numbers of CD8+, CD4+, and CD3+ TILs within tumours were significantly associated with better disease-free survival (DFS; p < 0.05) and overall survival (OS; p < 0.05). Additionally, increased presence of FOXP3+ TILs was linked to worse DFS and OS (p < 0.05). In multivariate analyses, higher CD8+ TIL density remained an independent predictor for improved DFS (HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.39 - 0.82, p = 0.004) and OS (HR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.43 - 0.91, p = 0.013). There was significant heterogeneity among studies; however, subgroup analysis by RT dose showed that CD8+ TIL levels had a stronger impact on DFS in high-dose compared to low-dose groups (interaction p = 0.004).
        Conclusion: Our findings suggest that TILs play a crucial role in determining the response to RT in rectal cancer. High levels of CD8+ TILs are associated with favourable prognosis regardless of the RT dose used. This information may help clinicians make more informed decisions about patient management and personalised therapies. Future prospective trials should validate these results and investigate potential mechanisms underlying the observed associations between TILs and RT efficacy.

title: Microbiome characterization of patients with Crohn disease and the use of fecal microbiota transplantation: A review.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic inflammatory condition predominantly affecting the intestines, encompassing both ulcerative colitis and Crohn disease (CD). As one of the most common gastrointestinal disorders, CD's pathogenesis is closely linked with the intestinal microbiota. Recently, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has gained attention as a potential treatment for CD, with the effective reestablishment of intestinal microecology considered a crucial mechanism of FMT therapy. This article synthesizes the findings of population-based cohort studies to enhance our understanding of gut microbial characteristics in patients with CD. It delves into the roles of "beneficial" and "pathogenic" bacteria in CD's development. This article systematically reviews and compares data on clinical response rates, remission rates, adverse events, and shifts in bacterial microbiota. Among these studies, gut microbiome analysis was conducted in only 7, and a single study examined the metabolome. Overall, FMT has demonstrated a partial restoration of typical CD-associated microbiological alterations, leading to increased α-diversity in responders and a moderate shift in patient microbiota toward the donor profile. Several factors, including donor selection, delivery route, microbial state (fresh or frozen), and recipient condition, are identified as pivotal in influencing FMT's effectiveness. Future prospective clinical studies with larger patient cohorts and improved methodologies are imperative. In addition, standardization of FMT procedures, coupled with advanced genomic techniques such as macroproteomics and culture genomics, is necessary. These advancements will further clarify the bacterial microbiota alterations that significantly contribute to FMT's therapeutic effects in CD treatment, as well as elucidate the underlying mechanisms of action.

title: A review of cutting-edge biomarkers for diagnosing coronary artery disease.
abstract: Chronic coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a significant global healthcare burden. Current risk assessment methods have notable limitations in early detection and risk stratification. Hence, there is an urgent need for innovative biomarkers that facilitate the premature CAD diagnosis, ultimately leading to reduction in associated morbidity and mortality rates. This review comprehensively examines recent advances in emerging biomarkers for CAD detection. Our analysis delves into various aspects of these biomarkers such as their mechanisms of action, roles in the pathophysiology of the disease, and different measurement techniques employed in clinical practice. Comparative assessment of biomarker performance between CAD patients and control groups was also presented relying on their sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve at specific cutoff points. In this regard, prominent biomarkers including Tenascin-C, IL-37, PTX3, transthyretin, soluble interleukin-6 receptor α, and miR-15a are identified as having high diagnostic potential for chronic CAD that indeed showcase promising performance metrics. These findings underscore the role of novel biomarkers in enhancing CAD risk stratification and improving patient outcomes through early intervention. However, the pursuit of an ideal and inclusive biomarker continues due to the multifaceted nature of CAD. Future randomized controlled trials are essential to bridge the gap between research findings and clinical practice in order to augment the practical application of these biomarkers in routine healthcare settings.

title: Evaluation of an online Cardiometabolic and Weight Loss Program. A mixed methods study.
abstract: Risk factors contributing to cardiovascular diseases (CVD) can be addressed through behavior modification, including changes in diet and physical activity. In 2021, The Wellness Institute (WI), located at Seven Oaks General Hospital, created a virtual cardiometabolic risk reduction program in response to COVID-19 pandemic public health restrictions, encompassing virtual health coaching and lifestyle education. The objective was to evaluate the acceptability, adherence, efficacy and engagement of the WI online cardiometabolic and weight loss program. The study followed a mixed methods quasi-experimental design. A total of 93 participants enrolled. Quantitative measures including anthropometrics, blood chemistry, and lifestyle were assessed for changes via paired t-tests at baseline and 16 weeks. Qualitatively, short answer questionnaires and three focus groups were completed to understand participants' experiences and program acceptability. We combined qualitative and quantitative data for analysis. Seventy-three participants (64 female, 87.7%) completed the final study visit (age 58 ± 11 years, weight 98 ± 20.9 kg). Of those, 98% attended all coaching sessions, would recommend the program, and reported the coaching sessions helped them stay motivated. A reduction in weight (5 ± 9 kg, p<0.001), systolic blood pressure (6 ± 10 mmHg, p<0.001) and diastolic blood pressure (4 ± 8 mmHg, p<0.001) were observed. Lifestyle factors also improved, including increases in physical activity (p<0.05). Most participants adhered to the program and found it acceptable. Completion was associated with an improvement in weight and blood pressure. These findings highlight the potential of virtual programming to contribute to improving lifestyle and health. Clinicaltrials.gov (ID# NCT04784624CT).

###### Abstract

Introduction: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death worldwide; however, most people do not meet recommended guidelines for healthy living. Virtual interventions offer potential solutions to address this issue by reducing barriers to accessing care and promoting remote engagement. The purpose of this randomized controlled trial was to investigate the effect of a comprehensive virtual intervention on improving cardio-metabolic risk factors compared to usual care.

Methods: This study included adults (N = 392) aged ≥ 18 years who had at least one cardio-metabolic risk factor or a family history of diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. Participants were randomly assigned into either the intervention group receiving personalized coaching through a mobile app, telehealth sessions with healthcare professionals, and educational materials or the control group which received standard care. Both groups completed self-assessments every three months over a year. Primary outcomes were changes from baseline to 12 months in body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1C), triglycerides (TGs), high density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), smoking status, and physical activity level. Secondary outcomes included patient satisfaction, acceptability, completion rate, and compliance with medication regimens.

Results: Attrition rates between groups did not differ significantly (intervention: n=149, 38%; control: n=160, 41%). Between-group differences in mean change scores favored the intervention group for BMI (-1.4 kg/m² vs -0.3 kg/m², p < 0.001), WC (-3.7 cm vs -1.4 cm, p < 0.001), SBP (-6.3 mmHg vs -1.1 mmHg, p < 0.001), and DBP (-3.7 mmHg vs -1.0 mmHg, p < 0.001). Improvements were also noted in secondary outcome measures such as increased physical activity levels (intervention: +525 steps/day vs control: +231 steps/day, p<0.05). Patient acceptance and completion rates were high within both groups (>90%), and no significant difference was detected between them. Smoking cessation attempts and successes were similar across groups. However, more intervention participants reported being prescribed new medications (p<0.001).

Discussion: Our results demonstrate that a comprehensive virtual intervention can lead to improvements in various cardio-metabolic risk factors when compared to standard care alone. The use of technology and personalized coaching may help overcome common barriers to engaging in behavior change programs, thereby contributing to better health outcomes. Future research should focus on optimizing virtual interventions to maximize their impact while minimizing resource requirements.
